test_title: RRB NTPC - Graduate 2025 (CBT 2) Advanced Full Test - 04
subject: general
question: The average speed of Gaurav during a two-way journey is 15 km/h. If he walked a distance of 20 km every hour while going, then his speed while returning will be:
solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

**Average Speed** for equal distance (two-way) = 2xy ÷ (x + y)

Given: **Average Speed** = 15 km/h, **Going Speed** (x) = 20 km/h

15 = (2 × 20 × y) ÷ (20 + y)

15 × (20 + y) = 40y ⇒ 300 + 15y = 40y ⇒ 25y = 300 ⇒ y = 12 km/h

**∴ The correct answer is 12 km/h.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Going Speed** (v₁) = 20 km/h (since he walks 20 km every hour)

**Average Speed** (Vₐvg) = 15 km/h

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e92cedad65df74a2f5aa13b7dd64bdaaac10d59bc476eaa3e02cfe29f6017aff.png] 

**Formula Used:**

Average Speed = **Total Distance** ÷ **Total Time**

For two equal distances: Vₐvg = 2v₁v₂ ÷ (v₁ + v₂)

**Calculations:**

⇒ 15 = (2 × 20 × v₂) ÷ (20 + v₂)

⇒ 15 × (20 + v₂) = 40v₂

⇒ 300 + 15v₂ = 40v₂

⇒ 40v₂ − 15v₂ = 300

⇒ 25v₂ = 300

⇒ v₂ = 300 ÷ 25

⇒ v₂ = 12 km/h

**∴ The correct answer is 12 km/h.**

**__Additional Information__**

Average Speed for Different Distances

If a person covers distances d₁, d₂ at speeds v₁, v₂, then Average Speed = (d₁ + d₂) ÷ (d₁/v₁ + d₂/v₂).

Harmonic Mean

For equal distance segments, the **average speed** is always the **Harmonic Mean** of the individual speeds.

Relative Speed

When two objects move in opposite directions, relative speed = s₁ + s₂. In the same direction, relative speed = |s₁ − s₂|.</p
